'''''Sedum hispanicum''''', the '''Spanish stonecrop''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=SEHI|taxon=Sedum hispanicum|accessdate=20 December 2016}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Crassulaceae]].

==Description==
''Sedum hispanicum'' is a [[Glabrousness|glabrous]] or somewhat pubescent annual, 5–15 cm tall. Its stems branch. Its linear leaves are alternate, 7–10 mm long and rounded. Its flowers are usually six-parted, sometimes 7–9-parted, arranged in unilateral cymes. Its sepals are ovate-acute. Its white petals have a purple midrib, and are 5–7 mm long, lanceolate and acuminate. Its carpels are stellate. It flowers from March to June.<ref name=Tohme14/>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Sedum hispanicum'' is [[Native species|native]] from south-central and southeastern Europe to Iran and the Arabian Peninsula. Notwithstanding its specific epithet ''hispanicum'', this stonecrop is not native to Spain.<ref name=POWO_275520-1>{{Cite POWO|title=''Sedum hispanicum'' L..|id=275520-1|access-date=2024-06-24|mode=cs1}}</ref> It thrives in loose rocky soil with plenty of drainage.<ref name=Tohme14/>
